stimulus.source_note: Anonymous 18th-century casta painting, public domain; Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: This 18th-century casta painting labels the child 'cambujo,' the offspring of a mulatto father and a 'china' (mixed-ancestry) mother, one of dozens of such precise labels. It shows the father holding the child while the mother prepares food at a table.

stem: The existence of so many specific categories is best understood as evidence of which colonial concern?

options.text: The drive to fix each person's legal and social status by ancestry, even as mixing continued.

options.misconception: Treats social labels as a scientific study.
options.text: A scientific program to study human biology and heredity in the colonies, sponsored by the Crown.

options.misconception: Reads multiplying labels as proof of stability.
options.text: Proof that colonial racial categories were stable, fixed, and never changed over time.

options.misconception: Turns a system that created distinctions into one that erased them.
options.text: An official campaign to eliminate all racial distinctions in colonial society.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
